prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a rear-end collision. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1479; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
- The repair labor hours are a little high for this damage.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
text: The rear bumper cover is cracked across the center and the left tail lamp housing is broken, with the trunk lid showing a crease along its lower edge. The damage pattern lines up with the reported impact, and the frame rails show no sign of sway. A few older scratches on the lower quarter panel may predate this loss and have been noted separately. The repair plan calls for replacing the bumper cover and tail lamp assembly, straightening the trunk lid, and refinishing the affected panels. The billing reviewed so far shows no repeated charges. Labor hours appear slightly high for this scope of work and should be checked against standard repair times before approval.
